BRAD HALPERN  RAY PEARL  NED E DAVIS  KELLY HONIG  SUSAN McSWEENEY

  AGENDA
  Regular Meeting of the City Council
  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE
  City Council Chambers
  31200 Oak Crest Drive

  Wednesday, July 13, 2022 - 6:30 p.m.

  Written comments may be sent to the City Clerk's Office at antoinette@wlv.org no later than
  12:00 p.m. on Wednesday, July 13, 2022. Written comments will be summarized during the
  meeting.

  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS:

  The Public may join this meeting virtually or attend in-person in the Council Chambers.

  Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, City Council members and staff may be participating
  in this meeting via teleconference pursuant to Government Code Section 54953(e).

  Please click the link below to join the webinar:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82741645273
  Webinar ID: 827 4164 5273
  One Tap Mobile:
  +16699009128,,82741645273# or +16694449171,,82741645273#
  Telephone:
  +1 669 900 9128 or +1 669 444 9171 or +1 346 248 7799 or +1 253 215 8782

  Teleconference participants will be muted until recognized at the appropriate time by the Mayor.

  In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-related
  modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or services,
  please call the City Clerk’s office at (818) 706-1613 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

  Any disclosable public records related to an open session item on a regular meeting agenda and
  distributed by the City to the City Council less than 72 hours prior to that meeting are available for public
  inspection at City Hall (31200 Oak Crest Drive, Westlake Village) during normal business hours.
 CALL TO ORDER: 6:30 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers McSweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tem Pearl,

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

APPROVAL OF MINUTES:

Minutes of June 22, 2022 Joint City Council and Homeowners Association
Representatives Meeting and the June 22, 2022 Regular City Council Meeting.

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

1.  Presentation - 2022 Quarterly Business Recognition Program by the City of
  Westlake Village and the Greater Conejo Valley Chamber of Commerce - MC2
  Wholesale

PUBLIC COMMENTS: Members of the public may address the City Council on items not on the
printed agenda. Please observe the time limit of three minutes. Members of the public may offer comment
telephonically or otherwise electronically by using Zoom teleconference service options as listed on Page
1 of this agenda. When attending in-person, complete a Speaker Card and submit it to the City Clerk prior
to the meeting starting.

COUNCIL RESPONSE:

STAFF COMMENTS:

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS: Reports on City Council Committee meetings held.

1.  ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE REPORT - City Council to direct staff to proceed
  with the issuance of the Landscape Maintenance Request for Proposals as
  presented.

PUBLIC HEARINGS: None

CONSENT CALENDAR: Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and
will be enacted by one motion and one vote. Unless otherwise requested by a Councilmember, there will
be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed from the
Consent Calendar and will be considered separately.

  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective July 15, 2022 in the amount of
  $866,802.37
 CONSENT CALENDAR (continued)

  GENERAL BUSINESS:

  1. ASSEMBLY BILL 361 FINDINGS FOR SPECIAL BROWN ACT
  REQUIREMENTS FOR TELECONFERENCE MEETINGS - City Council make
  the following findings so that teleconference meetings of the City Council and
  the City’s committees can continue to be conducted pursuant to the AB 361
  special Brown Act requirements: the City Council has reconsidered the
  circumstances of the COVID-19 state of emergency; and state and local
  officials continue to recommend measures to promote social distancing.
  2. REDESIGNATION OF LEAGUE OF CALIFORNIA CITIES VOTING
  DELEGATE FOR ANNUAL CONFERENCE - Designate Councilmember Ned

  NO. 2006-0003-DWQ - Approve the update of the Sewer System Management

  5. ACCEPTANCE OF AGOURA RD NORTH SIDE – BUS STOP TO GAS

1.  COVID-19 TEMPORARY OUTDOOR DINING AND BUSINESS OPERATIONS

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

Presentation of 2022 Quarterly Business Recognition Program was rescheduled to a
future meeting date as MC2 Wholesale was unable to attend.

PUBLIC COMMENTS: None

COUNCIL RESPONSE: None

STAFF COMMENTS:

Deputy City Manager Eskandar presented a COVIO update, stating City staffing is also
impacted by the current surge, and encouraged residents to be diligent in their efforts to
remain healthy. If the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health issues any
updated COVID Health Officer Orders due to the current COVID surge, updates will be
provided to our residents.

City staff and community volunteers were thanked for their assistance with the 4th of July
parade and fireworks show. Upcoming concerts in the park and a movie in the park were
announced.

Stonehaus was thanked for hosting the "Coffee with a Deputy" event. Lost Hills
Motorcycle Deputies conducted a 2-hour traffic saturation operation last week, to
reinforce safe driving practices and cite individuals for speeding antj traffic violations,
which resulted in 46 issued citations.

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

Councilmember Honig reported attending the Field Day for the Amateur Radio Club on
June 25, which illustrated how important the amateur radios are, especially in the event
of an emergency.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  July 13, 2022  3

  COUNCIL COMMENTS (continued):

l  Mayor Halpern reported reading a Los Angeles Times article about other cities conducting
  pedestrian safety projects like Westlake Village.

  Mayor Halpern stated Westlake Village recently lost four very involved volunteers, who
  all made a huge impact on the City and will be missed:

  •  Don Meyer was the 2020 Westlake Village Senior Citizen of the Year, in addition
  to being on the Community Fund Advisory Committee (2013 and 2014) and the
  Cultural Recreation Advisory Board (2018-2020) and very involved with the Yacht
  Club.
  •  Joyce Prouty was the volunteer City Historian since April 1988 where she oversaw
  the City's Historical Preservation Program.
  •  Suzanne Gallant was a member of the Cultural Recreation Advisory Board for 17
  years (2005-2021 ). She is best known for participating and knitting at meetings.
  •  Doris Rufner was the first City Historian (1984-1987) starting the City's historical
  program. Doris was also a 'First Lady' of Westlake Village when her husband
  served as Mayor.

  Mayor Halpern thanked the residents and staff for their participation in the July 4th parade
  and fireworks event.

  CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  1.  ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE REPORT

  Engineer Hughes reported that the Environmental Committee (Councilmembers
  Mcsweeney and Davis) met on June 28, 2022 to discuss the Citywide Landscape
  Contractor Request for Proposal (RFP) and the initial sidewalk design along
  Lindero Canyon Road from Whim Drive to Hedgewall and from Baronsgate Road
  to Agoura Road. The Environmental Committee recommended bringing the items
  to City Council for approval of the RFP and input on the sidewalk design.

  For Citywide Landscape (RFP), staff is proposing the same standard of care and

j  adding in the requirements for elimination of gas powered leaf blowers and two-
  stroke gas engines, following the American Green Zone Alliance (AGZA)
  recommendations for Level 1 and Level 2 certification. Achieving AGZA Level 1
  certification is key to achieving City Council sustainability goal. The RFP will
  address the certification in each of the years of the contract:
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  July 13, 2022  4

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS (continued):

  Year 1 (Oct 2022 -  Eliminate Two-Stroke Leaf Blowers by Jan 1, 2023 and
  June 2023)  all Other Two-Stroke Equipment by July 1, 2023 to
  achieve Green Zone Level 1 Certification (Base Bid)

  Year 2 (July 2023 -  Continue Green Zone Level 1 Certified (Base Bid)
  June 2024)  Optional: Eliminate Gas-Powered Equipment by July 1,
  2024 (additional scoring points for providing this option)

  Year 3 (July 2024 -  Continue Green Zone Level 1 Certified (Base Bid)
  June 2025)  Optional: Continue Green Zone Level 2 Certified
  Optional: Eliminate Gas-Powered Equipment by July 1,
  2025 (additional scoring points for providing each option)

  Staff anticipates bringing a contract to award in Fall 2022.

  Council discussion on two-stroke and four-stroke leaf blowers.

  Councilmember Honig moved to direct staff to proceed with the issuance of the
  Landscape Maintenance Request for Proposals as presented. Councilmember
  Davis seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl, and Mayor Halpern
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

  Mayor Halpern declared the motion passed 5-0.

  City Engineer Hughes presented the initial sidewalk design from along Lindero
  Canyon Road from Whim Drive to Hedgewall and from Baronsgate Road to Agoura
  Road. An easement will need to be obtained from Canyon Oaks Homeowners
  Association (HOA) to allow for adequate meandering of the sidewalk. Staff will
  engage with the Westpark HOA as an easement has already been obtained and
  will coordinate the final design for the meandering sidewalk segment and their
  driveway entrance.

  Council discussion on removal of trees and new tree wells to be added including
  planting magnolia trees.

1.  COVID-19 TEMPORARY OUTDOOR DINING AND BUSINESS OPERATIONS
  PERMITS: RESOLUTION NO. 2265-22

  Planning Director Forbes reported on consideration for a fifth permit extension.
  Temporary outdoor dining and business operation permits were issued due to
  COVID by the City Manager in May 2020 and ratified by City Council. City Council
  has issued four extensions, with the current Resolution set to expire August 31,
  2022.

  Staff reported that currently seven restaurants and breweries, 1 private club and 1
  dance studio still operate under temporary permit. Staff presented options for
  possible extension dates and advised that the Land Use Committee (Mayor Pro
  Tern Pearl and Councilmember Honig) recommended extending through January
  2, 2023 and directing staff to develop a permit program to allow for outdoor dining
  to continue indefinitely where appropriate and that the permit program would
  address safety and aesthetic issues.

  Council discussion on the extension date and it was determined that February 1,
  2023 would be the new date to allow staff time to develop a new program and
  develop all procedures associated.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved to Adopt Resolution No. 2265-22 titled, 'A
  Resolution of the City Council of the City of Westlake Village Extending COVID-19
  Temporary Outdoor Dining and Business Operations Permits to February 1, 2022'
  and that the City Council direct staff to return with recommendations for a program
  to allow outdoor dining on an ongoing basis. Councilmember Honig seconded the
  motion.
